title: The Queen of the Earth's Tremors
paragraphs: “What’s up? Are you giving up already?”
“Well, if I get used to it, there’s no point, right? From now on, I’m going to use some more advanced techniques!”
“Hmm…”

With that, the panda did a backflip, causing bamboo to appear right where he stood. He shifted his weight onto it, causing it to bend, and leaped upward, lunging toward Éclair. It’s just like a cannon. This is an attack only possible because the panda is round and massive.
“And then… Whoa! Whoops!”
As the panda speaks, several bamboo stalks shoot out from Éclair’s blind spot. It seems the panda intends to immobilize her.
“Even though the mechanism is the same, the bamboo appears with such versatility—attacking, obstructing, supporting… Is it handling all of that? I’m genuinely impressed.”

Éclair tightened her grip on her sword and used the bamboo as an axis to roll, turning it into a shield against the panda’s claws as it lunged at her. With a series of cracking sounds, the panda’s downward-slashing claws shattered the bamboo it had conjured with Magic. That’s quite a powerful attack.
However, it fell just short of reaching Éclair. From there, Éclair channeled Magic into her sword and thrust forward with great force.
“Your fighting style may be unassuming, but you sure know how to handle yourself. I never would’ve thought you’d be able to use bamboo like that.”

With a thud, the panda caught Éclair’s thrust with its claws while using several bamboo stalks as a shield; Éclair deflected the panda’s claws by firing a beam of light Magic. Then the panda even attempted a sweep, but Éclair anticipated it, lifting her leg to dodge while simultaneously launching a counter-kick at the panda’s supporting leg. The panda dodged that instantly as well.
The situation is evenly matched. With a light “whoosh,” they both stepped back slightly, then broke their stances and brushed the dust off their bodies.
“I understand you’re skilled. I’ve seen a mercenary’s fight firsthand.”
“A knight’s ‘noble’ fighting style just looks clumsy to me. But since you managed to parry my attacks cleanly, your skills seem solid.”
“Hmph… I’m sorry, but I believe courtesy should be upheld. It’s probably because you’re a mercenary that you prefer to attack from blind spots.”
“Éclair, aren’t you going to get angry at Panda’s attack?”
It seems the match has come to a temporary conclusion. So, here’s my question.

“...It could be a tactic to cover up a lack of skill with underhanded tricks. But in Larsazusa’s case, I sensed movements based on years of experience, always keeping in mind situations that work to his advantage. I suppose this is the art of survival as a mercenary.”
“Well, he can’t afford to get injured in a way that even healing magic can’t fix. It’s only natural he’d use any means necessary to avoid that.”

“If he’d done this while claiming to be fighting fair and square, I’d have found it unpleasant too. I also hate it when people rely on sheer level advantage to make themselves look stronger than they are, just to cover up their inexperience. Above all, I’d be furious if someone said one thing one moment and the opposite the next, depending on the situation.”

You mean that guy, don’t you? The one whose name starts with “Ta” and ends with “To.” By the way, it seems that was the attack Father took from Ren during the first world loop. I remembered it because there was a time when Ren was confessing with a gloomy expression.
“You mean the kind of guy who preaches chivalry during a duel, but when cornered, breaks the rules and ends up bringing up the mercenary thing?”
“Ah, yes! But didn’t Lord Larsazusa clearly declare that he was fighting as a mercenary? So I don’t find it offensive either.”
That’s exactly it. Ren’s behavior when he gets carried away is similar. Back then, Ren was strangely intent on outwitting his opponents.

To someone with true strength, those strange movements are a clear sign that he’s up to something. When cornered, a guy like that will try to pull off a brute-force move or unleash Skills to save himself. I’m sure he’d use one without hesitation even in a match where Skills are banned, if he looked like he was about to lose.
“Even though I never said anything about fighting ‘fair and square,’ there sure are a lot of knights who love to preach chivalry, aren’t there?”
“Where do you think I’m from?”
Éclair comes from a noble family in Melromarc that tried to build friendly relations with Demi-Humans and Beastmen. I see—so she was familiar with Demi-Human combat styles to some extent.

“If I judge things solely by human standards, I’ve had enough experience to know I’ll take unexpected hits. If you try to keep me at a distance by firing Magic from afar and running around, I won’t exactly be calm… but if that happens, I’ll just fight back.”
“I might do that, depending on the situation. But I’ll at least judge whether the opponent is the kind who’d go for it.”
“Hmph… You shouldn’t put yourself down like that.”
“I just don’t like fighting like a knight, that’s all.”
That’s the kind of banter Éclair and Panda were exchanging.
“Alright then, Elmero. It’s your turn next.”
“…Honestly, I’m not really fond of senseless battles.”
“That’s exactly why I’m telling you—you haven’t been acting like a goody-two-shoes lately just to imitate the Shield Hero, have you?”
Panda was calling him out with a look of utter exasperation. Does that mean he’s usually considered barbaric?
“Sigh… I guess I have no choice.”
Zou reluctantly got to his feet and stepped forward to take Panda’s place and face Éclair.
“Aren’t you tired from fighting Rasa?”
“No need to worry.”
“Fine, I’ll go… but this time, I’m going bare-handed.”
Does Zou intend to go easy on Éclair?
“What do you usually use?”
“You’ll understand once you see me fight.”
“I see… Well then, I’ll watch.”
Éclair lowers her center of gravity and assumes a fighting stance, ready to battle at any moment.
“How does Zou fight, anyway?”
“Her nickname is the ‘Queen of Earthquakes,’ so I guess it has something to do with that?”
“That’s right. I’m not one to talk—I’m the one who summons bamboo forests—but honestly, teaming up with Elmero is a hassle, so I don’t really like it.”
Panda says this as she slumps down listlessly. …She’s resting quite a ways behind us, isn’t she?
“Well then… let’s settle this…”
“Go!”

At Zou’s command, Éclair dashes toward her. She intends to quickly get around her side and launch an attack. But Zou swings his arm around, turns toward Éclair, and stomps the ground powerfully. Thud! The sound was several times louder than before, and the ground around us shook. A tremor rippled out from Zou’s position, and the vibrations reached even us, who were just watching from the sidelines.
"Whoa—"
Éclair is starting to lose her balance from the jolt. Of course, she regains her footing immediately, but the elephant has turned completely to face her head-on, so she couldn’t attack from the side.
"Haa!"
And with that, the elephant swings its leg upward and charges straight at Éclair.
“Ugh!”
The movement itself isn’t that fast, but because of its massive size, Éclair has to dodge widely or it’ll get hit.
“Not done yet!”
The elephant immediately changes direction and charges again. The ground continues to shake with a thud, thud. Because of that shaking, Éclair seems to be having a hard time running.

“Well, I think you’ve got the gist of it by now, right? Elmero, you see, basically fights using a strategy where he corners his opponent by creating massive ground tremors with Magic. He fights with a very offensive mindset.”
“It’s shaking pretty hard, isn’t it?”
“I think it’s done with earth-based Magic, don’t you think?”
“Elmero can cast it very frequently. I believe the Magic he’s using is called ‘Fast Earth Search’—it’s a Magic that causes a slight shockwave.”
“‘Fast,’ you say?”
It’s a beginner-level Magic. For one, it seems to have quite a powerful effect.
“It’s a weak Magic that uses your feet as a medium to cause slight vibrations in the surrounding area. But when Elmero uses it, it turns out like that.”
When a heavyweight like Zou uses it, it creates a rumbling that hinders the movements of those around him, doesn’t it?
“What is that Magic actually meant to be used for?”
“It’s useful for finding monsters hiding underground. As a side effect, it lets you know what’s buried in the ground around you.”
“So dowsing is its original purpose? Using it like that is pretty amazing, I guess.”
“Gaelion wouldn’t have any trouble with that opponent.”
Rival says this while showing off a tiny feather. Isn’t that just because you can fly?
“Well, Gaelion-chan, you see…”
“Well, I’m sure anyone who can use wind magic wouldn’t think twice about it. All they have to do is lift her up a little.”
“In a game, it’s all about type advantages, right? But it’s not just that, like with Lars-chan, is it?”
“That’s right. Well, as for me, I can summon a bamboo grove or just cling to a bamboo stalk—I can handle anything that way.”
“They say to take shelter in a bamboo grove during an earthquake… but I’m pretty sure that was a hoax, wasn’t it?”
“Is that so?”
I seem to recall hearing something like that, too.

“Well, yeah. If someone really goes all out with earth magic, the ground could get turned upside down, and we’d get buried along with the bamboo grove. The roots aren’t that strong. But the bamboo itself is fine even when it shakes, so I can use that motion to fly around.”
Ah, so you’re saying a panda can use the bamboo grove to fly around freely and attack an elephant from all angles. It seems like a pretty adaptable way to fight.
“I’m looking forward to seeing how that knight holds his own against Elmero.”
“When he’s up against Elmero, Eclair’s sword looks like a toothpick.”
Just as we were talking about that, Éclair leaped toward the elephant and, timing her charge with the elephant’s charge, cleared the gap by landing on its back.
“Whoa!”
But the elephant extends its trunk and tries to grab her.
“Not a chance!”
Éclair swings her sword, slashing at the elephant’s trunk. The elephant pulls back just slightly, allowing Éclair to break free.
“I’ve heard that fighting super-heavyweight Beastmen is a struggle… but this really is hard to attack… If I’d been caught, I’d have had a hard time breaking free.”
“Heh heh heh… So, how are you going to attack?”
It’s as if the elephant’s cat-like facade has slipped away; it’s wearing a condescending expression. You know, there’s a definite “dominant” vibe about it.
“Going head-on is a bad move. It’s obvious they’ll use not only their arms but even their trunk as a weapon… It’s like fighting an opponent with three arms.”
“So what are you going to do, then?”
“I’ll do this! Don’t think a mere earth tremor can stop me!”

Éclair charged head-on at the elephant, and just as it was about to slam her with both hands and its trunk, she accelerated even further… then slid right under the elephant’s legs. She immediately slashed at its legs with her sword.
“Ouch!? You got me!”
“Not yet!”

Éclair then moved to get behind the elephant and launch a follow-up attack. But something astonishing happened. Spikes shot up from the ground behind the elephant and counterattacked Éclair just as she was about to strike.
“Huh!?”
“There are plenty of opponents who try to slip under my legs. It’s been a while since I’ve faced an opponent who attacks with such good judgment and boldness!”
Every time the elephant stomped the ground, spikes continued to shoot out toward Éclair. She skillfully dodged them by backstepping, doing backflips, and somersaults.
“Is this a tactic you’ve faced many times before?”
“You bet.”
“It’s true—a reckless attack just gives your opponent a chance to strike back.”
“If you want to defeat me head-on, wouldn’t it be better to keep your distance and wear me down with Magic?”
“That’s certainly the safer approach. But I don’t think you’d be unable to handle that.”
“Hah! You really do understand me well.”

Zou responds as if to say Éclair’s answer was spot-on. At close range, he’ll hinder her movements and finish her off with a tank-like charge; at long range, he’ll take some other measure. If I get behind him, I’ll use Magic to cover my blind spots. If we were around the same level and had similar stats, it’d be a real struggle.
But why is that? I can’t help but picture Older Sister calmly and swiftly spearing Zou with a harpoon. I’d probably go in for the kill just as decisively.
“Elmero, your tone’s different.”
“That’s just his true nature. He’s a dissolute knight from Siltvelt who’s working as a mercenary, after all.”
“So normally, he’s more like Lars-chan?”
“That’s definitely right. That said, he seems to have a sense of chivalry in the strangest places—he’s a real pain in the neck.”
“What kind of person is he, exactly?”
“You can catch glimpses of a twisted life.”
Perhaps losing patience with Éclair’s constant evasion, Zou places his hand on the ground, uses Magic to pull a massive boulder out of the earth, and hurls it at her.
“Is that your countermeasure?!”
“That’s right. Do your best to dodge it!”

Éclair manages to dodge them somehow, but does she really stand a chance of winning like this? Zou keeps casting Magic to hurl boulders one after another, while repeatedly conjuring spikes from the ground to ensure Éclair has no time to rest. If there’s one thing that gives her a slight edge, it’s probably the fact that Zou’s movements are rather slow, don’t you think?
